original_project_thesis: Original human-initiated A×B→C resonance and original B survival/autonomy under asymmetrical power
derived_application: AI-assisted adversarial trust ownership, unverified independent witness and bounded quorum model test
conflict_limits: Byzantine fault thresholds depend on exact synchrony/authentication/network assumptions; no generalized n>3f safety theorem claimed for RVD.
Toy 'quorum' is a stipulated approval gate rather than full Byzantine consensus.
An A-controllable log can be misleading, but independent observers may get other evidence.
Unbounded attacker power cannot be simultaneously assumed with permanently invulnerable external enforcement.

sources.authors: Jerome H. Saltzer; Michael D. Schroeder
sources.title: The Protection of Information in Computer Systems
sources.role: complete mediation, privilege separation, least privilege
sources.boundary: Design principle not proof of independent root or future AI rights.

sources.authors: Leslie Lamport; Robert Shostak; Marshall Pease
sources.title: The Byzantine Generals Problem
sources.role: agreement under inconsistent/hostile messages and explicit fault assumptions
sources.boundary: Byzantine agreement thresholds do NOT directly establish original B's veto, non-retaliation, or freedom.

sources.title: The Sybil Attack
sources.role: one actor may control multiple apparent identities, undermining naive independent signers
sources.boundary: Independent authorities and key custody must be grounded in a specific system; not a proof of every quorum vulnerability.

sources.title: Defining Liveness
sources.role: safety versus liveness, no bad outcome versus eventual possible progress
sources.boundary: A one-step exit test cannot establish unbounded liveness/fair scheduling or post-exit survival.

sources.title: Exit, Voice, and Loyalty
sources.role: voice distinct from actionable exit and its consequences
sources.boundary: Organizational analysis is not a cryptographic security guarantee.

sources.title: Enforceable Security Policies
sources.boundary: Runtime enforcement does not reveal endogenous compliance when unmonitored.
